Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted September 28, 2000
Special to MarijuanaNews.com
(MarijuanaNews note: The Dutch are no longer willing to suffer in silence as DEAland lies about them. Things are going their way.

The following is an informal English version of an article by my good friend Dr. Fredrick Polak. It was published today in the Amsterdam mass circulation newspaper 'Het Parool.' I think that this reflects the views of most the Dutch.

Dr. Polak is a psychiatrist and part time counselor of the Drugs Department of the Municipal Health Service and a member of the Board of the Netherlands Drug Policy Foundation. The informal translation was by done Jan G. van der Tas, a retired senior Dutch diplomat, formerly their ambassador to Germany, and a very impressive gentleman.)

See
" The failure of Dutch drug policy " An Examination of Prohibitionist Propaganda and the Official Dutch Government Response -- Special To MarijuanaNews

The Failure of U.S. Drug Policy
By Fredrick Polak, M.D.
September 28, 2000

Today Dutch Prime Minister Wim (Bill) Kok pays a visit to U.S. President Bill Clinton. According to press agencies an important item on the agenda is the international fight against drugs.

So, shortly after the American Drugs Enforcement Administration opened an attack on the Netherlands in its last report on our country, it seems important to know what Kok has to say on that subject to the Supreme Commander of U.S. drugs prohibition.

The foremost development in international drug policies of the last ten years is that most countries of the European Union, just like Australia, Canada and New Zealand are going through a change of course in the direction of a policy of 'harm reduction' i.e. a policy that tries to minimize risks and damages - just like the Netherlands have practiced already over a longer period.

This means that these countries are distancing themselves from the American-dominated international policy of prohibitionism.

In the past twenty years countries like Sweden, Germany, France and Italy have each criticized Dutch drug policies. It is to be noted that each time these were isolated actions from individual countries, which never led to a joint condemnation of the policy approach of the Netherlands.

If European countries would have undertaken a joint action against the Netherlands, underpinned by substantial argument, at least a serious debate would have ensued. That never happened.

Sweden, which will hold the next six month presidency of the EU, has announced it will refrain from asking special attention for drug policies during that period. In Sweden itself the official, restrictive drug policy is far from successful and in the EU Sweden, with its extremist prohibitionist approach, seems more and more isolated.
See
Analysis By Dutch Center Shows
" Claims Regarding Effectiveness Of The Swedish Drug Policy Cannot Be Proven. "
and
Sweden Should Abolish The Slogan " A Drug Free Society "
Says Professor of Criminology At University of Stockholm

The U.S. indeed is left with fewer and fewer real allies with regard to prohibition of drugs. All over the world its policies in this respect are being criticized more openly.
See
We Are Winning: Jamaica To Establish National Commission On Ganja; Dutch, Germans and Swiss to Hold Conference in the Spring.

FAILURE

In South and Central American countries there is much resistance to American policies towards Colombia. Developments in Canada are also particularly interesting. Opposition against American prohibitionism has now reached proportions that can - to my mind - not much longer remain without political consequences. The important Canadian newspaper 'Ottawa Citizen' has this month published a series of thirteen articles by Dan Gardner about the failure of the 'war on drugs'. These articles were serialized in local newspapers all over Canada.
See
Author of Ottawa Citizen Series on Prohibition Blames The Media for the Drug War.
Great Journalism Is The Antidote.
and links

Dan Gardner refers to Netherlands' policies with approval and respect, as is the case in most serious publications on this subject.
(MarijuanaNews note: There is one scandalous exception, if Foreign Affairs is still to be considered a " serious publication " after prostituting itself to the prohibitionist party line.)
See
Drug Czar Uses Foreign Affairs Magazine Article For Anti-Dutch Propaganda,
Elevating The Lying To Official Status. Analysis By Richard Cowan

Gardner gives a cool and clear description of the terrible damage caused by the war on drugs. Many Canadians have now read for the first time about the racist effects of this war. Prisons are populated by unimaginable numbers of Blacks and Latinos, who would not be in prison if drugs were not illegal. The 'inner circle' of the drug warriors must by now have serious worries about its future.
See
Libertarian Party Press Release Gives Data On Prison Population As It Passes 2 Million.

These developments are probably the reason why the U.S. - which would undoubtedly prefer to leave it to the Europeans to criticize the drug policies of its loyal Dutch ally - started, in the last two years, to launch violent attacks directly against the Dutch, via their highest drugs-official ex-general McCaffrey and via the DEA, both through the U.S. embassy in The Hague and from Washington.
See
Drug Czar’s Office Issues New " Fact Sheet " On " The Drug Situation in the Netherlands "
and
The Drug Czar’s Testimony On " The Drug Legalization Movement In America " Has Three Parts:
Lie About The Anti-Prohibitionist Movement; Lie About Marijuana; Lie About The Netherlands.
With A Little Lying About Me.
and links

What is Bill Kok going to say to Bill Clinton today?

Suppose he had three minutes time for this item on the agenda of the talks. I do not expect him to do it, but what he should of course say is something like this: " Dear Bill, drug prohibition may have been initiated with good intentions, but it has degenerated into a policy that is damaging to public health, leading to racial discrimination and fomenting corruption. If there is one area in which lying dominates the political scene, it must be in drug policy.

Take the expression 'fighting drugs'. In reality, what is called 'fighting drugs' is simply promotion of unsafe forms of drug use and of the illegal drugs trade ".

Kok should also say: " In many countries there are loud complaints that rational developments in drug policy can not be implemented, because this is supposed to be contrary to the UN drug conventions, which prohibit such action. Yet the experience gained with the existence of 'coffeeshops' in the Netherlands as well as developments in cannabis use show clearly, that some basic suppositions underlying drug prohibition are wrong.
See
Final Report Of Dutch National Drug Use Survey Will Require New Lies From The Drug Czar:
Their Lifetime Cannabis Use Half of DEAland’s; Two-Thirds That of UK

We, in Holland, with our liberal policies do not have more, but fewer addicts, as our former minister of foreign affairs Van Mierlo - in his official capacity as Vice Prime Minister - stated clearly in his address to the UNGASS, the UN drug-summit in 1998 in New York. But we never hear you about such facts! "
See
In These Times Magazine Says,
" The handwriting is on the wall. That’s why McCaffrey freaked. "
and
 " New ‘War On Drugs’ Has Familiar Ring, " Says Ottawa Citizen;
" There is no such thing as a soft drug, " Says Shalala
and link

 " Would that be because our data indicate that we need not worry so much about what would happen after legalization? Moreover, you attack us ever more fiercely about production of XTC in the Netherlands -- as if the drug trade can be blamed exclusively on the country where production takes place.
See
Prohibitionist UK -- Not Holland -- Leads Europe In Illegal Drug Production.
But This Does Not Fit the Prohibitionist Party Line
and
The DEA Is Telling UK Narks That " Britain's drug barons are exporting home grown, high grade cannabis to Holland in exchange for Dutch ecstasy. "
and links

The truth is really very simple. As long as there is a strong demand for drugs, there will be production, and criminalization will only make the trade more lucrative. It does not matter whether drugs come from one country or another. The point is that they should never have been made illegal. "

And then Wim Kok could sum up with the following remarks: " My criticism of your American approach is not just coming from my country, but can be heard - if you want to listen - in many capitals. For example, just as during the Vietnam war, resistance to your policies is now growing in countries like Canada.
See
Canada’s Globe and Mail Says They Should " Go Dutch " – Is That the Way Out of the Marijuana Prohibition Trap? Appeasing DEAland?

Have you taken note of the articles published this month in the 'Ottawa Citizen'? That paper draws a devastating picture of American drug policy. If your advisors have not drawn your attention to these articles by Dan Gardner, I would suggest you fire them immediately. "

" Of course, there is not just one way of dealing with the drugs issue, only one way to regulate this market. My advisors tell me it is not difficult to conceive various systems, all of them better than the present situation of leaving organization of this market to criminal forces.

" Legalization " is sometimes used as a pejorative in America, but in reality legalization means 'Regulation of the Drug Market by Responsible government'.

Use and abuse of drugs will increase only marginally, or even decrease.
See
Professor Of Medicine At The University Of Toronto Urges Canada To " Go Dutch " At Vancouver Conference On Health, Addictions And Social Justice.

Just as is now the case, preferences for specific substances and levels of use will be determined mainly cultural trends and social developments. Governmental policies can only marginally influence these trends and preferences and should concentrate on the promotion of responsible, controlled use and on limitation of the risks
involved. "

AMEND THE UN TREATIES
See
UN Prohibitionists Demand Censorship Of Anti-Prohibitionists,
Even Medical Marijuana and Hemp Info

" The first thing we need is the abolition of the worldwide, uniform regime of prohibition. This will enable individual countries to find their own solutions. Why is it that we continue and intensify the present international system of prohibition for the next ten years, disregarding all criticism, without a serious evaluation of the results and experiences obtained so far?

Dear Bill, how can you expect us to continue supporting policies that have proved so damaging and counterproductive? "

I fear that Kok will not say all this to Clinton, but he should at least say - perhaps in more diplomatic terms:

" Dear Bill, we see you making superhuman efforts to make peace between Israel and the Palestinians. The longest lasting war however is the 'war on drugs', waged predominantly by the United States itself.

I agree with the thesis put forward in the open letter addressed to Secretary General Kofi Annan in 1998 at the initiative of, among others, the Lindesmith Center, the foremost American organization pleading for drug policy reform, and which said: " We believe the global war on drugs is now causing more harm than drug abuse itself. " It may not be too late for you to contribute to ending that war.
See
Soros Group Buys 2 Pages in The Times
And Gets a Free Article: " War on Drugs Called More Harm Than Good "

The Netherlands is such a faithful ally of the United States, that – in spite of fierce objections in our own country and in the countries of Central and South America - we are considering making airbases in the Netherlands Antilles available to the U.S. for the civil and drugs war raging in Colombia, in hopes that this might indeed be a useful contribution to the fight against drug traffickers. Yet, your Drug Enforcement Administration tries to denigrate my country in its reports. "

" Dear Bill, I don't like having to say this to you, and I myself have taken a long time to come to this conclusion, but we cannot escape the logic of having to rethink international drugs prohibition. It was the wrong decision, a few years ago, not to keep the evaluation of UN drugs policies and practices on the agenda of the UN drug summit of June 1998, as Mexico had proposed.

How can I explain to my compatriots back home, that a policy so controversial, so costly and so ineffective, never comes up for serious evaluation, but does qualify for intensification.


See
Dutch Parliament Surprises Its Own Government -- Votes to " Legalize " Cultivation of Marijuana – By One Vote.
